quickSummary: The circulatory system is closed and double-loop with a 3-chambered heart (2 atria, 1 muscular ventricle). Dorsal Sinus Venosus receives deoxygenated systemic blood (2 precavals, 1 postcaval) and houses the SAN pacemaker; ventral Conus Arteriosus carries blood into 3 arterial arches. Features both Hepatic (gut to liver) and Renal (hindlimbs to kidneys) Portal Systems. RBCs are large, biconvex, and nucleated.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Sinus Venosus is DORSAL (receives 2 precavals + 1 postcaval; contains SAN pacemaker). Conus Arteriosus is VENTRAL. RBCs are nucleated and biconvex.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FROG CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                             ▼                             ▼
THREE-CHAMBERED HEART          BLOOD COMPONENTS              PORTAL CIRCULATORY SYSTEMS
├── 2 Atria (Left & Right)     ├── Nucleated Oval RBCs        ├── Hepatic Portal System
├── 1 Ventricle                ├── WBCs & Thrombocytes        │   (Gut ──► Liver)
├── Sinus Venosus (Dorsal)     └── Plasma                     └── Renal Portal System
└── Conus Arteriosus (Ventral)                                    (Hindlimbs ──► Kidneys)
conceptBreakdown.content:
The circulatory system of *Rana tigrina* is closed, incomplete double circulation consisting of a 3-chambered heart, vascular trunks, lymphatics, and dual portal circuits.

### Heart Chambers & Accessory Structures
• **Two Atria**: Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the sinus venosus; left atrium receives oxygenated blood from pulmonary veins.
• **Single Ventricle**: Thick-walled muscular pump with internal muscular ridges called **Trabeculae / Columnae Carneae**.
• **Sinus Venosus (DORSAL)**: Triangular thin-walled chamber receiving 2 Precavals and 1 Postcaval vein; houses the cardiac pacemaker (**Sinu-Atrial Node / SAN**).
• **Conus Arteriosus (VENTRAL)**: Stout muscular tube arising from the ventricle base with a **Spiral Valve** guiding blood into three pairs of arterial arches (Carotid, Systemic, Pulmocutaneous).

DORSAL vs VENTRAL HEART
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  DORSAL ASPECT                                           VENTRAL ASPECT
  Sinus Venosus (Triangular)                              Conus Arteriosus

conceptBreakdown.content: Anatomical orientation is critical: Sinus Venosus is dorsal; Conus Arteriosus is ventral.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Hepatic & Renal Portal Systems
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Hepatic & Renal Portal Systems
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
RENAL PORTAL PATHWAY
                           
   Femoral & Sciatic Veins (Hindlimbs) ──► Renal Portal Vein ──► Kidneys
                                                                    │
   Heart (Sinus Venosus) ◄── Postcaval Vein ◄── Renal Veins ────────┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Hepatic Portal System**: Collects venous blood from stomach, intestine, pancreas, and spleen via the Hepatic Portal Vein and delivers it to the **Liver** for metabolic processing before entering the postcaval vein.
• **Renal Portal System**: Collects blood from the hindlimbs via femoral and sciatic veins and routes it through the **Kidneys** before reaching the postcaval vein (*unique to non-mammalian vertebrates; absent in mammals*).
• **Erythrocytes (RBCs)**: Large, oval, biconvex, and **NUCLEATED**, containing dissolved Hemoglobin.
